laneReturnLegalHold.why:
KNOWN_PREFILLS: AL6-03. CR-65's header caption box is printed "Court Case Number" with "(Assigned by Clerk)" directly beneath it. This packet writes matter.case_number into that box on nine of its eleven pages and leaves the identical box empty on the other two, and nothing in the held record says which case number the box is asking for.

What I measured in the delivered bytes. The caption box is filled on CR-65 pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 (AcroForm fields Text1, Text4, Text7, Text5, "Court Case Number", "Court Case Number_2" and "Court Case Number_4") and on C-10-CRIMINAL pages 1 and 2 ("Court Case Number" and "Court Case Number_2"). It is empty on CR-65 page 7, the certificate of service, where the field is CR-65:Court Case Number_3 at x=445.44 y=691.32 w=129.00 h=35.33 - the same x origin and the same 129.00pt width as "Court Case Number_2" on page 6 and "Court Case Number_4" on page 8, both of which are filled - and empty again on C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 (C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3). So the omission is not a different field or a different box; it is the same box on two of eleven pages. Both blanks are refused in production-field-map.json with role "protected" and refusalClass "signature_or_date_participant_completion", reason "signature or date field; never prefilled", which is not a true description of a caption box and, because the class is protected, keeps both out of the participant's "Blanks you must fill in" list. I rastered both pages of the boundary fixture at 150 dpi and looked at them: page 1 shows CC-2024-000001.99 sitting directly above the printed words "(Assigned by Clerk)"; page 7 shows an empty ruled box in the same position.

The fact that makes this a real question rather than a tidy-up. CR-65 page 1 separately prints its own line, "COURT CASE NUMBER TO BE EXPUNGED:", with its own field (CR-65:Text3, x=257.20 w=287.32), and this packet fills that line with the same matter.case_number value it puts in the caption box. Two differently labelled places on the same page therefore receive the same number. If the form already has a dedicated line for the case number to be expunged, the separately labelled caption box marked "(Assigned by Clerk)" is most naturally the expungement case the clerk opens on filing - a number that does not exist yet when the packet is generated and that no participant fact can supply. But that is a reading of Alabama court-form practice, not a fact recorded anywhere in this repository, and this lane will not author it.

Why the held record cannot settle it. AL.memo.json track al-diversion records rules.filing, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver, rules.notice, rules.service, rules.participantSignature and rules.notarization, and not one of them addresses the caption box. No participantInput on the track collects an expungement case number, and none distinguishes the underlying criminal case number from a clerk-assigned one. The packet's own field map offers no justification either: the nine writes carry factId matter.case_number with no decision or authority recorded, and the two refusals carry a reason that is false of the field.

Either answer leaves a defect; only its direction is open. If the box means the expungement case number the clerk assigns, then nine pages of this packet - including CR-65 pages 1 through 6, which the petitioner swears to under penalty of perjury on page 6 - carry a number that is not the number the box asks for, and the repair is to stop writing all nine and name the box as clerk-completed. If the box means the underlying criminal case, then CR-65 page 7 and C-10-CRIMINAL page 3 are wrongly blank, the page-7 refusal reason is false, and the repair is to write those two and reclassify them. The defect is certain; which repair is correct is not, and this lane does not choose between them. AL6-01 and AL6-02 are both genuinely gone from these bytes, and every other proof obligation this lane can settle from the record passes, so AL6-03 is the whole of the hold.

What would unblock it. A legal-design answer recorded in AL.memo.json - not in a lane return, a build script or a status file - stating whether CR-65's "Court Case Number (Assigned by Clerk)" caption box takes the underlying criminal case number or the expungement case number the clerk assigns on filing, and whether the same answer governs the identically captioned box on C-10-CRIMINAL. An owner or Alabama counsel establishing that one sentence makes the remaining work mechanical: whichever way it goes, the fix is a field-map change plus a refusal-class correction on CR-65:Court Case Number_3 and C-10-CRIMINAL:Court Case Number_3, and the packet can then be rebuilt and independently re-read. Nothing else about these six families is waiting on it.

failedObligations.finding: AL6-04, new here and decisive. CR-65 Section V is a conjunctive sworn certification - "AND ALL OF THE FOLLOWING HAVE OCCURRED. If you have not checked all eight boxes, the conviction is not eligible for expungement" - and the packet ticks all eight on the participant's behalf: Check Box10.6 on page 3 and Check Box11.0 through 11.6 on page 4, all under factId route.selection, on a petition sworn on CR-65 page 6. I rastered page 4 and read the eight printed lines against AL.memo.json track al-pardoned-felony. That track records eligibleDispositions ["a felony conviction for which a pardon has been granted"], exclusions [] (empty), waitingPeriods [] (empty), and only four participantInputs: pardonDate, restorationLanguage, firearmRightsExcluded, countyOfFiling. Six of the eight ticks therefore assert facts the route never establishes and never asks about: 11.1 "One hundred eighty days have passed from the date of the issuance of the certification of pardon" (no waiting period is recorded at all); 11.2 "the conviction is not a violent offense, as provided in Section 12-25-32"; 11.3 "not a sex offense, as provided in Section 15-20A-5"; 11.4 "not an offense involving moral turpitude, as provided in Section 17-3-30.1 ... and I have not been arrested for any offense, excluding minor traffic violations, 15 years prior to the filing of the petition"; 11.5 "not a serious traffic offense, as provided in Article 9 of Chapter 5A of Title 32"; 11.6 "At the time of the offense, I was not operating a commercial motor vehicle or was not holding a commercial driver license or commercial learner permit". A seventh, 11.0 "All civil and political rights that were forfeited as a result of the conviction have been restored", is contradicted by the track's own stop condition "The pardon withholds firearm rights and the restoration question controls" - the route expressly contemplates that this box may be false. Only 10.6, the certificate of pardon with restoration of civil and political rights, is the route's defining disposition. The comparison that proves this is not a general objection to conjunctive ticking: the sibling al-misd-conviction-set ticks its seven Section II boxes and every one of those seven IS backed by a memo exclusion, waiting period or participant input. Here six are backed by nothing. The eight-box list is source-authored, hardcoded as FAMILY_CONFIG["al-pardoned-felony-set"].selected in scripts/build-census-v1-al-diversion-set.mjs line 56, and assertRepairInvariants checks nothing about whether a ticked box is supported by the record. Telling the participant in step 3 to "confirm every condition printed in CR-65 Section V" does not cure ink already sworn on their behalf. This is the AL6-01 defect class - a semantically unsupported write into a sworn field - surviving the AL6-01 repair, with all nine counters at zero.

failedObligations.finding: This is the question this lane was asked to answer, and the answer is that the gap is real. The Colorado Judicial Department publishes JDF 491, 'Guide to Sealing Non-Conviction Records (simplified process)', at revision R: August 7, 2024 — the same revision date as both bound forms. Its step 2, headed 'File the Request — File these forms into your criminal case', names four forms with no branch and no condition between them: JDF 477 Motion, JDF 492 Order (just do §§ A-C), JDF 493 Notice (Just do §§ A-C), and JDF 478 Order (just do §§ A-C). Page 2 confirms it is one process, for cases ending in acquittal, a completed diversion agreement, a completed deferred judgment or a vacated conviction, under C.R.S. §§ 24-72-705 and 707 — the same statute and the same dispositions as this route. The packet delivers two of those four. JDF 492 and JDF 493 appear NOWHERE: not in the delivered packet, not in the packet-set manifest's components, not in the track registry entry, not in any file in the family directory (grepped), and not anywhere under STATES/CO in the master library, so they are a source-acquisition gap as well as a component gap. Nothing records the absence — there is no missing-component note, no open source item, no conditionDescription and no sentence in the participant guide telling a filer that the court's own guide names two more documents. The delivered guide instead states without qualification that 'This packet is two Colorado Judicial Department forms, filed together'. This lane read JDF 491 itself rather than a summary of it; its digest is 79dca4e720161b68ae74a8973392bbe22c05f565f704c609ec7cc7da0fcd3685 at STATES/CO/03_INSTRUCTIONS/CO__INSTRUCTIONS__JDF-491__guide-to-sealing-non-conviction-records__REV-2024-08-07__EN.pdf. This lane does not conclude that JDF 491 is right and the manifest wrong; it concludes that two committed sources disagree about what this route owes, that the disagreement is recorded nowhere, and that a route sells only what a record proves it delivers.

Two defects on the order the judge signs, both invisible to every counter because every value is present, non-empty, inside its declared write rect and equal to its expected value. FIRST, a value written into a field about something else. JDF-478 draws four separate fields in section 2c and each carries its own tooltip in the form's own metadata: '∆ Street Address' — "Enter the Defendant's street address.", '∆ City', '∆ State' and '∆ Zip'. The packet writes participant.street_address into '∆ Street Address' as the full concatenated value '412 Cherry Creek Way, Denver, CO 80202' and ALSO writes Denver, CO and 80202 into the three dedicated fields, so the delivered page 4 reads 'c) Mailing Address: 412 Cherry Creek Way, Denver, CO 80202 / City: Denver ST: CO Zip Code: 80202' and the city, state and ZIP are each printed twice on the proposed order. On the boundary fixture the duplication is a whole line long: the street field carries '1188 Upper Notch Crossing Road, Apartment 14B, Colorado Springs, Colorado 80921-2214' beside '∆ City' Colorado Springs and '∆ Zip' 80921-2214. The combined form is correct on JDF-477, whose field is captioned 'Current Mailing Address: (with city/state/zip)' and carries no tooltip — so the same fact is right on one form and wrong on the other, and the map's own label for the JDF-478 write is the printed caption 'Mailing Address' rather than the widget's declared purpose, which is how it read clean. This family's own municipal sibling writes street-only into the equivalent JDF-686 field with city, state and ZIP separate, so the correct behaviour exists in the same cohort. SECOND, a value that contradicts the field's own printed instruction. '∆ State' declares "Enter the state (use two letter abbreviation) in the Defendant's mailing address." and the boundary fixture writes 'Colorado'. It fits the 33.1 pt field and renders cleanly, so no geometry check sees it. Placement itself was verified for all 17 canonical and 16 boundary writes by reading the delivered pages with pdftotext and matching each value to the printed caption beside it, and every drawnText equals its expected value; the failure is which field the value went into and in what form, not where on the page it landed.

Four of the seven requiredBeforeFiling items in the controlling packet-set manifest reach the delivered guide neither verbatim nor in substance, and two of the four are substantive participant obligations rather than record boilerplate. Missing entirely, tested by literal substring match and then by keyword search of the whole delivered guide: (1) 'Obtain Colorado criminal-history report. Request a criminal-history report from CBI and attach it if the form requires it.' — the strings 'criminal-history' and 'criminal history' occur ZERO times in participant-instructions.md; the CBI appears only as an agency to list and notify, never as the source of a report the participant must obtain. (2) 'Check your answer to "How did the case end?" against Colorado criminal-history report, and correct the packet if they disagree.' — absent; the participant is never told to check the packet's account of how the case ended against anything. (3) 'The source review does not state a notarization requirement.' — the string 'notari' occurs zero times, and JDF-477 section 10 is a declaration under penalty of perjury, so whether it must be notarised is a question a filer will actually have. (4) 'The source review does not address a fee waiver.' — 'waiver' and 'waive' occur zero times. Of the three that do land, the movant-signs item and the signature-and-date item are carried in substance as steps 4 and 5 of 'What you must do before you file', and the fee item is carried better than verbatim — 'Ask the clerk what fee applies, if any. failedObligations.finding: THE BRIEF ASKED WHICH OF THE TWO THIS IS. IT IS BOTH, AND THE OBLIGATION MEASURES WHAT IS PRESENT RATHER THAN WHAT WAS DISCLOSED, SO IT FAILS. What is delivered: attachments 4, 5 and 6 of in_conviction_serious_felony-set - the Appearance, Form ACR and the Confidential Information Form - and nothing else. What the three bound routes require and nobody renders: ten components. I verified the builder's claim independently rather than taking it, by searching the packetComponents of all 346 families in MASTER_QUEUE for the three track ids; the only components any family declares for in_conviction_serious_felony, in_collateral_action or in_supplemental_order are the three attachments this family delivers. So no family in the queue builds the serious-felony petition, its proposed order, its attachment-3 or its instructions component, and neither of the other two routes has a single component declared anywhere. A participant on any of these three routes cannot file with this packet: it contains no petition and no proposed order, and an Appearance and a notice of exclusion filed alone commence nothing. THE DISCLOSURE IS EXEMPLARY AND I RECORD IT IN FULL. participant-instructions.md opens 'What is in this packet, and what is not', its second heading is 'Read this first: these three forms are not the filing', and it says in terms 'The petition itself is not in this packet, and neither is the proposed order. If you file only these three sheets, you have not asked the court for anything', and then that neither of the other two routes' own filings is built here either. filing-instructions.md carries a section headed 'What this packet does NOT contain', and production-field-map.json lists all ten under componentsOfThisFamilysOwnRoutesThatNothingBuilds. That disclosure is why this is a queue scope decision - widen this family or open two more - rather than a build error, and the build lane says so itself. ONE MORE THING I MEASURED THAT BEARS ON THE SCOPE DECISION: three sibling Indiana families - in-conviction-felony-set, in-conviction-misd-set and in-conviction-d6-set - each deliver a COMPLETE ten-page packet whose pages 7-10 are these very same three documents, and they deliver them BLANK. I confirmed it by hashing the extracted text of every page of each: their page 8 is textually identical to this family's page 2, and their pages 7, 9 and 10 are the same three documents with 'STATE OF INDIANA ____________' and 'PETITIONER'S NAME: ______' unfilled. So the fill this family maps is genuinely owed work that nothing else does; it is simply attached to routes whose filings nobody builds.

No signature, signature date or court-only field carries a VALUE - both signature rules on the Appearance, the signature rule on Form ACR, all three cause-number lines and the full Social Security number box are empty on the delivered pages, and I confirmed each. THE FAILURE IS THAT FOUR CERTIFICATE-OF-SERVICE CONTROLS CARRY INK THIS BUILD DREW. A certificate of service asserts that service has happened; this family's own approval-request calls a ticked one 'the single worst defect this packet could carry' and asks a reviewer to confirm both boxes are empty on each of the two documents. They are not empty. On packet page 2 (the Appearance's certificate of service) and packet page 3 (Form ACR's), each of the four alternatives' checkbox widgets is flattened as an appearance whose entire content is '0.5 0.5 17 17 re s' - a stroked rectangle - and that rectangle is stamped onto the page. Proved against the pinned source, not inferred: rendering source page 2 and delivered page 2 at 200 dpi and differencing them gives 554 added dark pixels and zero removed, in exactly two hollow squares of 277 pixels at x 110.2-121.7pt, on a page that carries no value write at all; the crop shows the form's own checkbox with a second, smaller square drawn inside it. reports/actual-writes.json publishes refusedFieldsWithInk: [] for both fixtures and that is false as delivered.

EIGHT FLATTENED WIDGET APPEARANCES PER FIXTURE STAMP A RECTANGLE THE FORM DOES NOT PRINT ONTO THE DELIVERED PAGE. This is the same defect mo-art-xiv-marijuana-set was failed and repaired for - pdf-lib's default appearance provider reading /MK /BC for a widget with no usable /AP /N, with flatten then stamping the invention - and this factory's own scan-synthesized-widget-borders.mjs names the mechanism precisely. Measured, not inferred. (1) From the bytes: of 46 flattened appearance XObjects per fixture, 20 carry show-text, 18 are empty and 8 contain a path-paint operator and no text at all; their entire decompressed content is '0.5 0.5 9.599 11.8762 re s' at four page-1 checkboxes and '0.5 0.5 17 17 re s' at two page-2 and two page-3 checkboxes. Identical in canonical and boundary. (2) From the pixels, against the pinned source: differencing 200-dpi renders of source page 2 against delivered page 2 gives 554 added dark pixels and 0 removed, in exactly two hollow 277-pixel squares - and delivered page 2 carries no value write, so those pixels are the whole of what this build added to it. Page 3 gives the same two. Cropping the page-1 'I will accept service at the above email address' box shows the shape: the source draws the form's own checkbox; the delivered page draws that box AND a second, offset square inside it. Every other limb of this obligation is clean and I record it: no run is wider than its own box in either fixture (measured with Helvetica advance widths, including the boundary fixture's 39-character hyphenated name and 60-character email, which the finalizer shrinks to 8pt and 7.5pt and which fit), every one of the 13 ink runs is inside its own widget rect and appearance BBox, and no two runs overlap. FIX80's cohort does not list this family only because the scan predates its build; five of its Indiana siblings ARE in that cohort, with 659 exposed widgets between them.

39 of the 40 stop conditions the three bound routes declare are carried VERBATIM, and I checked each one string by string against IN.memo.json rather than reading a count: in_conviction_serious_felony 13 of 13, in_supplemental_order 13 of 13, in_collateral_action 13 of 14. THE ONE THAT IS MISSING IS THE ONLY ONE UNIQUE TO ITS ROUTE: 'The court finds the collateral action does not relate to the expunged matter.' It is absent from participant-instructions.md, absent from filing-instructions.md and absent from all four delivered pages - I searched for it verbatim and for 'does not relate' and 'collateral action does not relate' in every delivered byte, and there is no occurrence and no paraphrase. The guide's stop list under 'When this is not a do-it-yourself matter' prints exactly the thirteen the serious-felony track declares, introduced as 'The record names these as the points where the filing these forms accompany stops being a self-help matter' - but three routes are bound to this family and the guide gives each of them its own filing, fee, notice and service section, so a participant on the collateral-action route reads a stop list from which their own route's distinctive condition has been dropped. Narrow, provable and worth naming so a repair carries it: the other thirty-nine need no work. (The guide claims no count, so this is a shortfall against the record rather than a false statement about itself.)

laneReturnLegalHold.why: SELF_HELP_STOP: The stated defect is repaired and I measured it: all FIVE selfHelpStopConditions are printed verbatim, in the registry's own order, on the composed filing-instructions page and again in participant-instructions.md (checked string by string after whitespace normalisation), and the Dotson screen sits as a hard gate BESIDE the Part 1 basis election in three places -- step 2 of 'WHAT YOU DO, IN ORDER' on the facing composed page, step 2 of 'What you must do' in the guide, and 'The choices that are yours'. What blocks the obligation is what that gate SAYS against the pinned form. The packet instructs: 'if your charge was dismissed after a stipulation or after a judicial finding of facts sufficient for guilt ... do not tick that box and do not file this petition.' The pinned CC-1473 Rev. 07/26, page 1, Part 1, prints the opposite inclusion in the same packet: the 'otherwise dismissed' basis expressly covers 'a charge that is dismissed after a plea or stipulation of the facts that would justify a finding of guilt pursuant to Sec. 19.2-298.02'. A participant in exactly that population is told by the official form that the basis reaches them and by the packet not to file. Which governs is a legal question about Dotson and Sec. 19.2-298.02 that a reader may not settle by measurement, FIX89 itself returned it undischarged as BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT, and the standing VF01 row already carried SELF_HELP_STOP as a blocked legal obligation. It is recorded blocked here rather than passed.
